name: Maximum Flow and Minimum s-t Cut
problem_statement: Given a capacitated graph and distinct source and sink vertices, compute a maximum feasible flow and a minimum-capacity separating cut. With optional vertex capacities, the cut can contain both original edges and capacity-limited vertices.

normalization: Treat edge weight as capacity; reject negative capacity.
Collapse parallel edges between the same ordered pair by summing capacity.
Treat an undirected edge request as two opposite directed edges with equal capacity.
Remove self-loops; they never contribute to an s-t flow or cut.

problem_inputs.name: capacity_mode
problem_inputs.description: Use declared edge weights or treat every edge as unit capacity.

problem_inputs.name: vertex_capacities
problem_inputs.description: Optional nonnegative per-vertex throughput limits; unspecified vertices are unbounded. Explicit source/sink limits are respected. Native JSON encodes the typed-ID map as an array of {vertex, capacity} records, preserving the distinction between numeric and string IDs.

problem_inputs.name: return_cut_side
problem_inputs.description: Whether to return the source-side vertex partition induced by the minimum cut.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: Whether an approximate max-flow value with a disclosed bound is permitted.

required_outputs.name: max_flow_value
required_outputs.description: Value of the maximum feasible source-to-sink flow.

required_outputs.name: min_cut_value
required_outputs.description: Combined capacity of cut edges and cut vertices; equals max_flow_value. Without vertex capacities this is the edge-only cut capacity.

required_outputs.name: min_cut_edges
required_outputs.description: Original edges crossing the residual split-network cut. Together with min_cut_vertices they separate source from sink; in edge-only mode these edges alone form the cut.

optional_outputs.name: flow_assignment
optional_outputs.description: Feasible capacity-bounded flow on each original edge, with parallel flow restored. Undirected inputs have two oriented assignment records per non-loop edge; source and target disambiguate the shared original edge ID.

optional_outputs.name: source_side_vertices
optional_outputs.description: Original vertices whose input copy is residual-reachable from source. With vertex capacities, this includes cut vertices; split_source_side records both input/output reachability.

optional_outputs.name: approximation_bound
optional_outputs.description: Certified relative or additive gap for an approximate result.

optional_outputs.name: min_cut_vertices
optional_outputs.description: Capacity-limited vertices whose input copy is residual-reachable but output copy is not. Required with vertex capacities; empty in edge-only mode. May contain an explicitly limited source or sink.

optional_outputs.name: split_source_side
optional_outputs.description: When return_cut_side=true, vertex ID with input_reachable and output_reachable in the residual vertex-split network.

solution_semantics.objective: Maximize source-to-sink flow under edge capacities and optional vertex throughput limits. Vertex splitting defines the mixed cut; unspecified vertex capacities cannot constrain flow.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact mode requires optimal=true and max_flow_value == min_cut_value within tolerance.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Multiple minimum cuts may exist; return one unless alternates are explicitly requested.
solution_semantics.ordering: Not applicable; outputs are a value, an edge set, and optionally a flow assignment.

validation_rules: flow_assignment satisfies every original directed capacity, with opposite oriented assignments for undirected edges, and conservation at every non-terminal vertex.
Explicit vertex capacities bound throughput, including explicitly limited terminals.
The sum of capacities of min_cut_edges and min_cut_vertices equals min_cut_value; no cut vertex is unbounded.
max_flow_value equals min_cut_value exactly for an exact-arithmetic profile or within its declared numerical tolerance.
Removing min_cut_edges and min_cut_vertices eliminates every source-to-sink path; removal of an explicitly limited terminal is a valid vertex cut.
edge_cases: No directed path exists from source to sink: max_flow_value is zero and min_cut_edges is empty.
Source and sink are the same vertex is rejected as invalid input.
Disconnected or zero-capacity edges do not affect optimality but may affect returned flow_assignment sparsity.
Multiple minimum cuts of equal value may exist; any one is acceptable unless the caller requests the source-side-maximal or sink-side-maximal canonical cut.
An explicitly zero-capacity source or sink can give a zero-valued cut containing that terminal; source_side_vertices may then include a cut terminal, as defined by split reachability.

correctness: flow value agreement with exact oracle
